raw_comment:
I notice that the droughts are located in clusters. It also looks like the droughts almost trail to the east, maybe due to the rain shadow of mountains? The prevailing winds in the US go from west to east, so it seems to match.
I wonder what is different about those regions. Are they already desert? Is there a sudden area of lower elevation there? What is the atmosphere like above it? Is there a weaker area in the ozone layer?

My area occasionally gets hit by droughts, and is just southwest of one of the heavy drought areas. We get heavily affected by the lower moisture once the spring snow runoff is gone. 


America Going Dry: Why?
